Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: running JGR from server?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to speed up installation (and maintenance) of JGR in a lab of 24 machines.  My thought was to install R on a server and put a shortcut to that copy of R on each of the machines.  This works fine when I'm just running R, and it's nice because I can update packages on this single server copy.  But when I try JGR(), I get this:

> JGR()

Copy the following into WordPad and save as "jgrLaunch.bat"

set R_HOME=X:\Math\R\Rcurrent
set R_LIBS=X:\Math\R\Rcurrent\library
set R_LIBS_USER=X:\Math\R\Rcurrent\library
jgr-1_62.exe --rhome=X:\Math\R\Rcurrent --libpath=X:\Math\R\Rcurrent\library

Error in file(file, ifelse(append, "a", "w")) :
  cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(file, ifelse(append, "a", "w")) :
  cannot open file 'jgrLaunch.bat': Permission denied

If I do the same thing after I've first established write privileges to the remote directory, JGR() seems to execute fine but nothing appears on the local machine.  Perhaps JGR has launched on the remote server (X:\Math\R) but not on my local machine?

Do you have any suggestions?  Or perhaps any resources that you know about that might help us get JGR running from a remote copy?

Many thanks!
--Bill

____________________________
Bill Altermatt, Ph.D.
Department of Psychology
Hanover College

JGR gets the information about Java and R from the registry - that is the only way to locate things on Windows as there are no "standard" paths. So all you need to do is to make sure your remote R is registered on the local machine: in SOFTWARE/R-core/R there must be InstallPath entry with the path to R - check the machine that you used to install it for details.

Simon

Ok, great. Just for clarification - this is a known issue in Java 1.7. So far I have only seen it in the Oracle binary, so I'm somewhat surprised that the icedtea binary has the same problem. For the Oracle binary is it somewhat excusable, because they hard-code the Java location which is a-priori not known (1.6 did not make that mistake, though). But icedtea should know better ... Let me know if R 2.14.0 works, because the work-around assumes that the reported boot path is correct which it is for Oracle's binary, but I didn't see icedtea binary so I didn't check that one.

BTW: if you don't want to upgrade the whole R you can simply just copy over the most recent javareconf which you can find at
https://svn.r-project.org/R/trunk/src/scripts/javareconf

Thanks,
Simon
